<reason>CON preserved the key distinction between a shared vendor and a horizontal agreement. PRO asserted surveillance and discipline but never proved them for shared tools as a category, then narrowed its test to confidential pooling plus commitment and punishment—facts that already establish coordination. CON exposed that retreat and the circular burden-shift without abandoning scrutiny for genuine cartels.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: PRO's confidential-pooling-plus-discipline test is CON's evidence-first standard, not category-wide treatment as direct coordinators, and visibility or losing tenants is competition rather than cartel retaliation.</best_rebuttal>
